fields.Name: IT06 - RLS Multi-User Cache Isolation
fields.Description: Proves User A's RLS-filtered cache entry can never serve User B. RLS1: two distinct effective RLS clauses yield distinct cache fingerprints (the rls:<hash> segment of GenerateRunViewFingerprint). RLS2: on the server superset slot (TrustLocalCacheCompletely), User B's identical read is a separate cold slot — not a hit on User A's slot — and no A-scoped rows leak. RLS4: an empty effective RLS clause does not change the fingerprint (RLS-exempt users keep sharing slots) while a non-empty clause does — an always-runnable fingerprint invariant that holds even on databases with no two distinct RLS users. Two-user fixture is DISCOVERED (never minted) from the provider's RLS filters + the user cache; degrades gracefully (skip-as-pass) when the DB has only RLS-exempt admins. The #1 security item from the #2824 backlog.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Distinct RLS clauses => distinct cache fingerprints (empty clause => shared slot); User B never served from User A's slot; no cross-user rows.
